# Overview

This analysis explores fire exposure and sensitivity indicators for national parks, examining the distribution of values, comparing different scaling approaches (normalized vs. ranked), and evaluating transformation methods.

## Load Libraries and Data

```{r load-libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(corrplot)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)
library(knitr)
library(DT)
library(plotly)

# Load the datasets
fire_exposure <- read_csv("data/rapid/all/fire_exposure_2025-09-09.csv")
fire_sensitivity <- read_csv("data/rapid/all/fire_sensitivity_2025-09-09.csv")

```

## Data Overview

```{r data-overview}
# Basic info about datasets
cat("Fire Exposure Dataset:\n")
cat("Dimensions:", dim(fire_exposure), "\n")
cat("Parks:", n_distinct(fire_exposure$park_name), "\n\n")

cat("Fire Sensitivity Dataset:\n") 
cat("Dimensions:", dim(fire_sensitivity), "\n")
cat("Parks:", n_distinct(fire_sensitivity$park_name), "\n\n")

# Check for overlapping parks
common_parks <- intersect(fire_exposure$park_name, fire_sensitivity$park_name)
cat("Common parks between datasets:", length(common_parks), "\n")
```

```{r data-preview}
# Preview the datasets
kable(head(fire_exposure), caption = "Fire Exposure Data (First 6 rows)")

```

# Fire Exposure Analysis

## Distribution Analysis

```{r fire-exposure-distributions}
# Raw probability changes
raw_cols <- fire_exposure %>% select(contains("raw_fire_prob"))
norm_cols <- fire_exposure %>% select(contains("norm_fire_prob"))

# Create long format for plotting
exposure_long <- fire_exposure %>%
  select(park_name, contains("fire_prob_change")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -park_name, names_to = "indicator", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(
    percentile = str_extract(indicator, "p\\d+"),
    type = case_when(
      str_detect(indicator, "raw_") ~ "Raw Values",
      str_detect(indicator, "norm_") ~ "Normalized",
      str_detect(indicator, "rank_") ~ "Ranked"
    )
  )

# Distribution plots
p1 <- exposure_long %>%
  filter(type == "Raw Values") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, fill = percentile)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~percentile, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Raw Fire Probability Changes",
       x = "Raw Fire Probability Change", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- exposure_long %>%
  filter(type == "Normalized") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, fill = percentile)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~percentile, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Normalized Fire Probability Changes",
       x = "Normalized Fire Probability Change", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 1)
```

## Comparison: Raw vs Normalized vs Ranked

```{r exposure-comparison}
# Summary statistics
exposure_summary <- fire_exposure %>%
  select(contains("fire_prob_change")) %>%
  summary()

print(exposure_summary)

# Correlation between raw and normalized values
cor_matrix_p50 <- fire_exposure %>%
  select(raw_fire_prob_change_p50, norm_fire_prob_change_p50, rank_fire_prob_change_p50) %>%
  cor(use = "complete.obs")

corrplot(cor_matrix_p50, method = "color", 
         title = "Correlation: Raw vs Normalized vs Ranked (P50)",
         mar = c(0,0,0,0))
```

```{r exposure-scatter}
# Scatter plots comparing scaling methods
p3 <- ggplot(fire_exposure, aes(x = raw_fire_prob_change_p50, y = norm_fire_prob_change_p50)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Raw vs Normalized Fire Probability Change (P50)",
       x = "Raw Values", y = "Normalized Values") +
  theme_minimal()

p4 <- ggplot(fire_exposure, aes(x = norm_fire_prob_change_p50, y = rank_fire_prob_change_p50)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Normalized vs Ranked Fire Probability Change (P50)",
       x = "Normalized Values", y = "Ranked Values") +
  theme_minimal()

grid.arrange(p3, p4, ncol = 1)
```

# Combined Analysis

## Join Datasets

```{r combine-datasets}
# Join the datasets
combined_data <- fire_exposure %>%
  full_join(fire_sensitivity, by = c("wsd_source_id", "park_unit", "park_name")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(raw_fire_prob_change_p50) & !is.na(raw_wildfire_hazard_mean))

cat("Combined dataset dimensions:", dim(combined_data), "\n")
cat("Parks with both exposure and sensitivity data:", n_distinct(combined_data$park_name), "\n")
```

## Exposure vs Sensitivity Relationship

```{r exposure-sensitivity-relationship}
# Scatter plot of exposure vs sensitivity
p5 <- ggplot(combined_data, aes(x = raw_wildfire_hazard_mean, y = raw_fire_prob_change_p50)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Fire Exposure vs Fire Sensitivity (Raw Values)",
       x = "Raw Wildfire Hazard (Sensitivity)", 
       y = "Raw Fire Probability Change P50 (Exposure)") +
  theme_minimal()

# Same plot with normalized values
p6 <- ggplot(combined_data, aes(x = norm_wildfire_hazard_mean, y = norm_fire_prob_change_p50)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Fire Exposure vs Fire Sensitivity (Normalized Values)",
       x = "Normalized Wildfire Hazard (Sensitivity)",
       y = "Normalized Fire Probability Change P50 (Exposure)") +
  theme_minimal()

grid.arrange(p5, p6, ncol = 1)

# Correlation
cat("Correlation between exposure and sensitivity:\n")
cat("Raw values:", cor(combined_data$raw_wildfire_hazard_mean, 
                      combined_data$raw_fire_prob_change_p50, use = "complete.obs"), "\n")
cat("Normalized values:", cor(combined_data$norm_wildfire_hazard_mean, 
                             combined_data$norm_fire_prob_change_p50, use = "complete.obs"), "\n")
```

# Transformation Assessment

## Assess Data Distributions for Transformation Needs

```{r assess-transformations}
# Check skewness and consider transformations
library(e1071)

# Function to assess distribution and suggest transformations
assess_distribution <- function(data, var_name) {
  skew <- skewness(data, na.rm = TRUE)
  kurt <- kurtosis(data, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  cat("Variable:", var_name, "\n")
  cat("Skewness:", round(skew, 3), "\n")
  cat("Kurtosis:", round(kurt, 3), "\n")
  
  if (abs(skew) > 1) {
    cat("Highly skewed - consider transformation\n")
  } else if (abs(skew) > 0.5) {
    cat("Moderately skewed - may benefit from transformation\n")
  } else {
    cat("Approximately normal distribution\n")
  }
  cat("\n")
}

# Assess key variables
assess_distribution(fire_exposure$raw_fire_prob_change_p50, "Fire Exposure P50 (Raw)")
assess_distribution(fire_sensitivity$raw_wildfire_hazard_mean, "Wildfire Hazard (Raw)")
```

## Test Alternative Transformations

```{r test-transformations}
# Test different transformations
test_var <- fire_exposure$raw_fire_prob_change_p50[!is.na(fire_exposure$raw_fire_prob_change_p50)]

# Handle negative values if present
if(any(test_var < 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  # Shift to make all values positive for log transformation
  test_var_shifted <- test_var - min(test_var, na.rm = TRUE) + 1
  
  transformations <- data.frame(
    original = test_var,
    log_shifted = log(test_var_shifted),
    sqrt_shifted = sqrt(test_var_shifted),
    rank = rank(test_var)
  )
} else {
  transformations <- data.frame(
    original = test_var,
    log = log(test_var + 1),  # Add 1 to handle zeros
    sqrt = sqrt(test_var),
    rank = rank(test_var)
  )
}

# Plot transformations
trans_long <- transformations %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "transformation", values_to = "value")

ggplot(trans_long, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.7, fill = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~transformation, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Effect of Different Transformations on Fire Exposure P50",
       x = "Transformed Value", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# Calculate skewness for each transformation
trans_skewness <- sapply(transformations, function(x) skewness(x, na.rm = TRUE))
cat("Skewness after transformations:\n")
print(round(trans_skewness, 3))
```

# Recommendations

## Summary Statistics Table

```{r summary-table}
# Create comprehensive summary
summary_stats <- combined_data %>%
  select(raw_fire_prob_change_p10, raw_fire_prob_change_p50, raw_fire_prob_change_p90,
         norm_fire_prob_change_p10, norm_fire_prob_change_p50, norm_fire_prob_change_p90,
         raw_wildfire_hazard_mean, norm_wildfire_hazard_mean) %>%
  summarise_all(list(
    mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
    median = ~median(., na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = ~sd(., na.rm = TRUE),
    min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
    max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE),
    skewness = ~skewness(., na.rm = TRUE)
  )) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  separate(variable, into = c("indicator", "statistic"), sep = "_(?=[^_]*$)") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = statistic, values_from = value)

DT::datatable(summary_stats, options = list(scrollX = TRUE))
```

```{r extreme-parks}
bottom_exposure <- combined_data %>%
  arrange(raw_fire_prob_change_p50) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  select(park_name, raw_fire_prob_change_p50, norm_fire_prob_change_p50, rank_fire_prob_change_p50)

cat("Top 10 Parks by Fire Exposure (P50):\n")

cat("\nBottom 10 Parks by Fire Exposure (P50):\n") 
kable(bottom_exposure)
```

# Conclusions and Recommendations

Based on this analysis:

## Key Findings

1.  **Distribution Characteristics**:
    -   Examine the skewness values and distribution plots above to determine if transformations are needed
    -   Compare how well normalized vs ranked scaling preserves relationships
2.  **Scaling Method Comparison**:
    -   Correlation analysis shows the relationship between raw, normalized, and ranked values
    -   Consider which method best suits your analytical needs
3.  **Exposure vs Sensitivity Relationship**:
    -   Evaluate the correlation between fire exposure and sensitivity indicators
    -   Determine if they measure independent aspects of fire vulnerability

## Recommendations for Indicator Calculation

```{r final-recommendations}
# Based on the analysis, provide specific recommendations
cat("RECOMMENDATIONS:\n\n")

cat("1. DATA TRANSFORMATION:\n")
cat("   - Check skewness values above\n")
cat("   - If |skewness| > 1, consider log or square root transformation\n")
cat("   - Ranking may be most robust for highly skewed data\n\n")

cat("2. SCALING METHOD:\n")
cat("   - Normalized values preserve original scale relationships\n")
cat("   - Ranked values are more robust to outliers\n")
cat("   - Consider your intended use case\n\n")

cat("3. PERCENTILE SELECTION:\n")
cat("   - P50 (median) is most stable\n")
cat("   - P90 captures extreme risk scenarios\n")
cat("   - P10 shows lower-bound estimates\n\n")

cat("4. DATA QUALITY:\n")
cat("   - Check for missing values and outliers\n")
cat("   - Validate extreme values with domain experts\n")
```

# Compare Fire Sensitivity Methods

Calculate sensitivity adding "Moderate" category:

```{r}
whp_raster <- terra::rast("data/all/usfs_fire/whp2023_GeoTIF/whp2023_cls_conus.tif")


binary <- terra::ifel(whp_raster %in% 3:5, 1, 0)

# Process each water supply
results <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(water_supplies_buffer)), function(i) {
 
    # Calculate area-weighted % high/very high WHP category for water supply buffer
    
    ## pull out park shapefile and transform
    ws <- terra::vect(st_transform(water_supplies_buffer[i, ], crs(whp_raster)))
    
    # Extract values with cell overlap fractions
    extracted <- terra::extract(binary, ws, weights = TRUE, exact = TRUE)
    
    # weights column = fraction of cell in polygon
    total_weight <- sum(extracted$weight, na.rm = TRUE)
    coverage_weight <- sum(extracted$weight[extracted$class_desc == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
    
    percent <- (coverage_weight / total_weight) * 100
    
    # Create results tibble
    tibble(
      wsd_source_id = water_supplies_buffer[i, ]$wsd_source_id,
      park_unit = water_supplies_buffer[i, ]$park_unit,
      park_name = water_supplies_buffer[i, ]$park_name,
      raw_wildfire_hazard_mean = percent
    )
    
    
  }
  
  
  
)

# Calculate standardized indicators using helper function
final_results <- results %>%
  add_standardized_indicators("raw_wildfire_hazard")

filename <- file.path("data/rapid/outputs/", paste0("fire_sensitivity_moderate", Sys.Date(), ".csv"))
write_csv(final_results, filename)

```
